approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs. It samples breeding parents from high-score population groups, applies its existing crossover and mutations, and builds a surplus pool of fresh valid identities. A Gaussian process trained on all accepted raw scores uses count fingerprints and a Tanimoto kernel. For each evaluation slot it draws a correlated score function across that pool and picks the best still-available molecule. Real accepted outcomes alone update the model archive and score-ranked survivors. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled; ordinary mutations and their continuation remain active.
approach.novelty: Add incumbent-referenced expected batch improvement: reuse one fixed panel of joint posterior scenarios, begin every scenario at the best raw score already accepted, and choose each molecule for its remaining positive contribution to that batch improvement. This targets progress beyond the current best while accounting for score peaks covered by earlier batch choices. Earlier shared-panel and antithetic experiments maximized an unthresholded batch maximum under an older Parent. Current siblings have tested representation, predictive targets, generation, feedback and selector removals; none supplies a formally evaluated current-Parent unthresholded shared-panel control. This experiment therefore tests the complete new allocation rule against the Parent. The same-panel unthresholded comparison explains decision differences without claiming an isolated endpoint effect of the threshold.

observed_bottleneck: The successful allocator in n-62daf219c70a takes one masked winner from each independent joint posterior draw. Its raw-score count GP and complete fresh pool remain useful, but this rule does not explicitly value improvement above the accepted incumbent or the marginal improvement left after earlier batch choices. The current matched baseline completes all fifteen task/seed sessions with mean 0.5956696497334577 and seed population SD 0.02659287062806747. Removing active composite selection while retaining full generation and model computation in n-01b48dd09404 changes every batch set and loses 0.12438789088524467 in paired mean; its two improved zaleplon endpoints prevent a universal contribution claim. This supports changing acquisition within the retained model/pool boundary, not assuming a new utility will help. Historical n-9c0f6fa601f8 executes the 128-path unthresholded expected-maximum law, changes 434/435 same-panel batch sets and raises internal panel utility, yet its paired mean is -0.0003646022443066406 against n-559d25e9c9c7. Historical antithetic n-0db88abff519 changes 431/435 sets and raises its panel utility but loses 0.016104112533858978; it also has a distinct exact-zero mean completion rule. Both are executed counterexamples to endpoint benefit, and their analyses identify lack of an incumbent threshold as one unresolved mismatch, not a proven cause. They use the older exchange-containing count Parent and historical conditions, not the current code Parent/profile. Current rank-target n-ae12ccae8c7b loses 0.021067064526871015 despite more parent beats/incumbent updates, and magnitude-credit n-9d0376974738 loses 0.028995941477343672 despite larger eligible source gains. These results motivate one explicit accepted-incumbent acquisition test while rejecting local gains or internal sampled utility as substitutes for endpoints.
hypothesis: Replace successful independent-row posterior allocation with greedy incumbent-referenced expected batch improvement over one fixed 128-or-announced-batch-size shared joint posterior panel, using only the best previously accepted raw score and exact smallest-index ties.

finding_summary.headline: Incumbent targeting raises sampled batch utility, but smaller real gains lower all three seed means
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation mechanism executed and changed real decisions. All 435 frozen incumbents, 128-row posterior panels and 4,350 exact greedy choices passed independent reconstruction. There were 3,681 positive-gain choices and 669 exact-zero choices; 23 complete batches had zero sampled improvement from their first position. Every zero choice followed the registered smallest-index tie rule without a fallback. All 435 selected sets differed from the Parent rule on the same panels. Mean sampled batch-improvement utility rose by 0.005726: 371 batches improved, 64 tied and none declined. Against the unthresholded shared-panel rule, 343 sets changed and mean utility rose by 0.000256, with fifteen contrary losses.

Real progress moved the other way. Average realized batch improvement fell from 0.013351 to 0.011410. Advancing batches rose from 202 to 204 and sequential incumbent updates from 258 to 270, but mean positive batch gain fell from 0.028751 to 0.024331. Mean accepted offspring score also fell, from 0.385256 to 0.351177. All evaluations completed, yet final mean score fell from 0.595670 to 0.539394, a paired change of -0.056276 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.092867, -0.016706 and -0.059254. Nine task-seed endpoints declined and six improved, including all three median-similarity endpoints.

molecular.headline: Aryl amines and bridged lactams persist; an acyclic sulfur/urea chain leads one task despite zero sampled marginal gain
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives and all three issued Search seeds were inspected for Child n-8a62df15e51f and code Parent n-62daf219c70a. Each node has 4,500 evaluated records, including 4,350 optimizer products; every task contributes 900 records and 870 optimizer products. context.comparison establishes both complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing, with no profile mismatch or missing trajectory. All fifteen paired trajectories differ; common molecular identities retain consistent recorded scores. The actual resource receipt records three completed replicas with six CPUs, 16,000 MB and one A40 each. The supplied full-panel mean is 0.5393940797230263 versus 0.5956696497334577, with paired seed changes -0.09286669965406602,-0.016705653920698005 and -0.05925435645652999. All three median-similarity endpoints improve, while several other endpoints fall; these contrary cases remain in the per-task comparisons. These are recorded evaluation outcomes, not an activation, eligibility or component-contribution decision. The molecules remain rich in aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks: indole carboxamides, linked halogenated heteroaryls, cyclic and macrocyclic amines, ether/lactam bridges and aza-dicarbonyl cores. A conspicuous exception is an acyclic urea/enamide/ketone/thioaldehyde leader. Median heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25,37,29,31,26, versus Parent 25,33,31,30,27. The overall median is four perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Digest ring-string presence ranges from 0.8931 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string presence from 0.8034 to 0.9782; these are molecule-level text counters, not geometry or aromatic atom fractions. The lowest aromatic fraction belongs to the population containing the acyclic leader, so its ring-free chemistry must not be hidden by the overall ring-rich description. Within-seed upper-score neighborhoods are usually much narrower than the complete panel. Familiar functional groups coexist with chemical liabilities. Counts of optimizer molecules with N-halogen/O-halogen/O-O bonds are 437/109/75 for the Child versus 1,042/278/273 for the Parent. This decrease in specific motifs does not establish a global feasibility improvement: the Child has 147 molecules containing a ring carbon with at least two double bonds, versus 42 in the Parent, and also produces aryl cyanates, terminal C=S groups, N-S substitution, crowded aminals, short unsaturated rings and dense bridges. Not every carbon with two double bonds is the same kind of cumulene; the concrete cyclic carbon-chain examples are identified below. No Child evaluated molecule has a ring triple bond, but that is not evidence of its absence from unscored pools or the unchanged generator's support. There are 124 products with at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 99, alongside evaluated structures as large as 120 heavy atoms. All digest stereocentre-marker rates are zero, while RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,391 Child and 2,408 Parent optimizer rows. Ring perception, sanitization and a score do not establish a synthesis, stability, accessible conformation, safety or a preferred stereoisomer. Actual molecule provenance was joined through pool identity, emitted prediction, accepted score, survivor population and later parent reuse in all thirty logs. The Child and Parent each construct 69,600 pool records and evaluate 4,350 optimizer products. Every one of the 435 Child suggestions freezes its incumbent from the complete preceding accepted raw-score archive; all exact tied records and the smallest-serial representative match that history. The representative is an initial molecule in 17 batches and an earlier accepted offspring in 418; 53 batches have multiple incumbent ties. It is neither the generating-parent score nor a posterior prediction or future observation. The fixed recorded panel has 128 joint function-value rows in each batch. All active marginal vectors, masks, chosen identities and exact tie choices were checked against that panel without generating new draws or scores. The prediction mean and standard deviation remain raw-score moments; posterior_sample is a passive panel-row value, separate from the optimizing marginal increment. There are 3,681 positive-marginal and 669 exact-zero-marginal evaluated choices. The latter occur in 96 batches, including 23 wholly zero batches, and select the smallest remaining original pool index. This is normal finite-panel saturation, not numerical fallback; no fallback occurred. The zero cohort contains 70 acyclic products and 24 tiny fragments, but also substantial useful-scoring molecules: 59 beat their best generating parent, 14 exceed the batch's frozen incumbent, 11 update the running incumbent, 355 survive their batch, 119 remain in the final population and 205 are later bred. Only four of these zero-marginal choices have any panel row above the original incumbent; later marginal saturation can also occur after earlier choices already cover those rows. Zero finite-panel utility therefore does not show chemical absence or lack of real improvement potential. Two session leaders come from zero-marginal ties. The acyclic leader in seed 1 of the final task is evaluation 194, position 3/pool index 3 in wholly saturated batch 19. Its frozen incumbent is the earlier accepted evaluation 143 at 0.3487520004285424, drawn from 190 preceding accepted records; its generating parent is a different molecule at 0.2624259366847637. The leader scores 0.43419030554852406 after an append and ring opening. Seed 2/evaluation 158 is likewise a zero choice, scoring 0.4189666353060081 after a fluorine append to a small-ring dicarbonyl family. Both are molecular counterexamples to treating zero sampled marginal gain as useless chemistry, but neither identifies a beneficial causal contribution from the tie rule or the acquisition threshold. All 435 same-panel passive controls are available. The unthresholded rule changes its batch set relative to the actual choices in 343 batches; the independent-row rule changes all 435. Their complete sequences were checked on their own masks, separately from same-active-prefix diagnostics. Unevaluated alternatives receive no labels, chemical-outcome claims or hypothetical future histories. The actual scored Child has 632 best-parent beats and 270 incumbent updates versus Parent 629 and 258, while mean realized improvement over the frozen batch incumbent is 0.011410412713128188 versus 0.013350949610039598. Counts of local wins, internal panel utilities and selected chemistry are different observations; none alone explains the lower complete endpoints. Historical unthresholded n-9c0f6fa601f8 and antithetic n-0db88abff519 retain their original exchange-containing Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 and paired means -0.0003646022443066406 and -0.016104112533858978. Both had opposing seed effects; the antithetic variant also used a different zero-gain mean-completion rule. They are conditional counterexamples, not independent tests on the present exchange-free Parent. Current rank-target n-ae12ccae8c7b and magnitude-credit n-9d0376974738 likewise retain their negative endpoint results despite favorable local progress measurements. There is no formally evaluated current-Parent unthresholded sibling: this comparison concerns the complete incumbent-referenced shared-panel rule versus independent-row allocation, and cannot split the threshold from the changed panel/batch law. Shared-Parent contrasts and later breeding ancestry do not establish additive efficacy or chemical mediation of terminal scores. Read-only reproducible audits are in .slots/r0019-01-improve-L01/molecular/. Full trajectory chemistry is in trajectory_chemistry_audit.json; allocation_exposure_audit.json joins actual history, choices and retained molecules; selected_chemistry_audit.json links positive/zero cohorts and leader provenance; historical_evidence_extract.json preserves the original sources and conditions. Only the immutable brief's canonical response_path contains this report.

per_task.generated_character: Better products are compact indole carboxamides with a separate phenyl or pyridyl surface and methoxy, methyl or vinyl substituents. The top fifty have 23-26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Seed 0's leader has an N-amino indole, bromomethyl group and fluorophenyl amide. Seed 1 has a vinyl/methoxy indole with an N-S-substituted pyridyl amide. Seed 2's 24-heavy-atom leader carries an enol-like vinyl alcohol and an amide nitrogen/methylene bridge spanning a pyridyl ring; its five perceived rings do not make this bridge a routine saturated amine. N-halogen bonds are much less prevalent than in the Parent: 128 versus 445 optimizer products, although still present in 19 of the highest fifty. Parent leaders used related aromatic carbonyl frameworks, including N-fluoro, N-hydroxyamide and diketone chemistry. The shift changes local liabilities without eliminating them.
liabilities: Bromomethyl substitution, N-amino indole, N-S-substituted amide and residual N-Cl/N-Br amides warrant distinct chemical scrutiny; they are not interchangeable with ordinary aryl halogenation.
The short amide-N/methylene bridge across a pyridyl ring constrains geometry. The leader’s enol-like group adds a tautomeric question that is not resolved by its recorded score.
missing_features: The small poor products lack the combined aromatic surfaces and compact carbonyl connection found in better molecules. The leading excerpt offers limited routine alternatives preserving that spacing without short pyridyl-spanning bridges, N-S/N-N substitution or halomethyl groups.
The enol-bearing and bridged products do not establish stable tautomeric or accessible three-dimensional alternatives. The scalar records identify no mandatory missing target-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.305105. The leaders reach 0.427621, 0.436954 and 0.447214. A more conventional vinyl/methoxy pyridyl carboxamide at seed 1/evaluation 178 already scores 0.423990, so neither N-S nor N-halogen substitution is required for every substantial score. In the bridged seed 2 family, the vinyl/methoxy product at evaluation 231 scores 0.445195, while the later carbonyl-free connection at evaluation 295 scores 0.326476 and the homologated carbonyl connection at evaluation 296 scores 0.315372. These associations favor a compact, correctly spaced aromatic/carbonyl arrangement, not arbitrary enlargement or loss of the carbonyl. NBr at seed 0/evaluation 292 scores zero. All three session leaders were selected with positive sampled marginal gain, but their molecule-score associations do not identify an acquisition-mediated functional-group effect. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.427621 versus 0.394051; 0.436954 versus 0.474117; 0.447214 versus 0.438973 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by multi-ring nitrogen-rich aromatic assemblies with halogen, carbonyl or thione substitution. Seed 0's leader combines a difluoro aminopyridyl/imidate region with a bridged N-rich dicarbonyl core and isobutyl substituent. Seed 1 instead reaches a 41-heavy-atom, four-aryl-ring assembly joined around a substituted alkene, with five halogens, an aryl O-C#N cyanate and an aryl formate ester. Related upper molecules retain fused lactone/thione heteroaromatics. Seed 2's leader has conjugated exocyclic connections, a dicarbonyl ring, heteroaryl amine and a graph-perceived pair of unsaturated four-member rings. The complete median size is 37 heavy atoms versus Parent 33; the upper fifty span 37-41 heavy atoms, while other evaluated assemblies extend to 120. The Parent's strong seed-0 family was smaller and also chemically problematic, with O-halogen/thione chemistry.
liabilities: O-C#N is an aryl cyanate linkage, not a carbon-bound nitrile. Thiones, imidates and conjugated exocyclic systems create distinct reactivity or stability questions.
Short-ring unsaturation, unspecified alkene geometry and extensively linked aromatic material complicate synthetic plausibility. High scores do not resolve these issues.
missing_features: Tiny floor-scoring products lack the extended aromatic and polar pattern of the upper families. Larger output does not show reliable retention of that pattern in compact, chemically ordinary alternatives.

The upper excerpt lacks demonstrated conventional replacements preserving its useful ring relationships while avoiding aryl cyanates, unusual short unsaturated ring connections or highly repeated assemblies. This is not evidence of their absence from unscored alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl/dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381. Child leaders score 0.596941, 0.629319 and 0.614689, while CBr and atomic fluorine examples remain at 0.5. The seed 1 terminal-alkene and internally substituted alkene examples at evaluations 284 and 291 both score 0.629279. Changing one peripheral aryl Cl to Br in the thione family at evaluations 245 and 278 also leaves its score at 0.626562. Thus the larger aromatic/heteroatom arrangement matters in the visible gradient, but these precise peripheral identities are not independently rewarded. The seed 2 late cumulated-chain product at evaluation 295 still scores 0.613971 despite its unusual unsaturation. All three leaders entered through positive-marginal allocation; the marked seed-0 loss remains visible rather than being replaced by the slightly improved seed-1 endpoint. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.596941 versus 0.856148; 0.629319 versus 0.624821; 0.614689 versus 0.617802 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: The stronger products already contain free amines and halogenated aryl surfaces. Seed 2's compact leader has only 21 heavy atoms: N-propylpyrrolidine linked to an aryl-substituted cyclobutene, with methoxy and aryl F. Seed 0 has two aromatic domains connected through an amine to a hydroxylated, crowded N-containing seven-member ring. Seed 1 leads with a ten-member amine/ether ring, phenol, aminoethyl substituent and a chlorophenyl methyl thioether. The top fifty have 21-28 heavy atoms and all have unassigned tetrahedral centres. The complete panel has 143 molecules containing a ring carbon with two double bonds, versus Parent two; these cyclic-cumulation intermediates are far more frequent than among the highest fifty. Parent leaders likewise contained aryl/basic-amine frameworks, often with more aromatic bulk; the whole-panel median changes from 31 to 29 heavy atoms.
liabilities: Small unsaturated rings and frequent cyclic cumulated double bonds raise geometry and synthesis questions; the compact leader still contains a cyclobutene and two unassigned tetrahedral centres.

Crowded aminal-like/hemiaminal centres, medium-to-large ring closure and thioether substitution need whole-molecule assessment. Some high-value structures are more conventional locally without making the entire panel routine.
missing_features: Poor examples lack the free/basic-amine arrangement present in stronger molecules, but the generator as a whole does not lack amine centres or saturated nitrogen rings.

The strong evaluated families lack explicit stereochemical definition at cyclic amine, cyclobutene and crowded N/O-adjacent centres. Less constrained ring alternatives preserving the same aryl/amine spacing are not systematically demonstrated by the leaders.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed 2 cyclobutene/tertiary-amine leader scores 0.999989, while its more heavily chlorinated/ brominated neighbor at evaluation 286 scores 0.996231. A sulfonylated pyrrolidine ketone at seed 0/ evaluation 15 scores 0.000212, and the trichloroaryl diol at seed 1/evaluation 78 only 0.002818. Within these samples, freely basic amines in substantial aryl arrangements associate with high values; halogenated aryl material or blocked ring nitrogen alone is insufficient. Seed 1/evaluation 271 is a recorded deletion product at 0.995351 from the cyclic-cumulene parent at evaluation 265, 0.986919. Conversely, zero-marginal seed 0/evaluation 80 is itself a difficult short-ring cumulene and improves the frozen incumbent from 0.331936 to 0.363416. Neither high real score nor a zero predicted marginal class certifies chemical feasibility. All terminal leaders were positive-marginal selections. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.971984 versus 0.999999; 0.995351 versus 0.996975; 0.999989 versus 0.999993 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: Better products combine substituted phenyl or quinoline surfaces with N-methyl lactam/dicarbonyl units, ether links and bridged medium-ring frameworks. Seed 0's leader has 35 heavy atoms and five perceived rings of sizes 6,6,6,7,8, combining two aromatic surfaces with a ketone/lactam system and N/O bridges. Seed 1's 29-heavy-atom leader links quinoline through O-N connectivity to a bridged imine/dicarbonyl aza-system; seed 2 has a related 33-heavy-atom hydrazine/N-O-containing family with eight- and nine-member rings. All highest fifty carry unassigned tetrahedral centres; none has O-halogen or O-O bonds and only one has N-halogen. This is a counterexample to describing all upper-score chemistry as dominated by reactive halogen bonds. The median is 31 heavy atoms versus Parent 30, with the same broad aromatic/lactam inventory but different bridges and linkages.
liabilities: N-O links, hydrazine-related N-N connections, imines and dense N/O bridges complicate stability and synthesis even where familiar lactams are retained.
Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 778 of 870 optimizer products; the absence of stereocentre tokens does not mean achiral chemistry.
missing_features: The small low-score products lack the combined aromatic and distributed carbonyl/lactam features of the better products. The upper families do not demonstrate a broad set of simpler, stereochemically defined cores preserving those relationships.
Dense bridges, N-O/N-N connections and medium-ring stereochemistry remain unresolved. No hidden target fragment or preferred configuration is established by the recorded scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.167839. Child leaders reach 0.234809, 0.224985 and 0.226526; ethylene and dichloromethane examples score zero. Seed 0's related more nitrogen-containing bridged product at evaluation 252 scores 0.227992. Retaining substantial aromatic and carbonyl architecture associates with the higher values, but the observations do not isolate a universally preferred nitrogen count or ring closure. All 870 optimizer choices have positive sampled marginal gain on this task, yet only some improve their real parent or incumbent. All three matched endpoints increase modestly; these gains remain alongside the full-panel losses. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.234809 versus 0.225840; 0.224985 versus 0.221410; 0.226526 versus 0.226003 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: This population spans chemically different solutions. Seed 0 leads with an N-S-substituted dicarbonyl bicyclic core, a fluorinated five-member imine ring and a fluoromethyl cyclopentadienol. Seed 2 leads with pyridyl and difluoro/aminoaryl groups on a dicarbonyl heterocycle fused to an unsaturated four-member nitrogen ring. Seed 1's highest product is entirely acyclic: a 24-heavy-atom chain containing substituted urea, ketone, enamide, terminal C=S, fluoropropyl acyl and an N-bound fluoro/chloromethyl centre. This ring-free leader is a real exception to the abundant cyclic output. The whole-panel median is 26 heavy atoms and one aromatic ring versus Parent 27 and three aromatic rings. N-halogen occurrence falls to 39 from Parent 476, but N-S chemistry, thiocarbonyl/enamide chains, small-ring strain and unspecified geometry remain. Parent leaders included N-F carbonyl/imino rings and a highly scored but difficult cyclic-cumulene family.
liabilities: The acyclic leader has a terminal thioaldehyde-like C=S and conjugated carbonyl/enamide chain, with unspecified alkene geometry and an unassigned fluoro/chloro carbon centre.

The cyclic leaders retain N-S substitution, imine/enol chemistry or an unsaturated four-member nitrogen ring. Fewer N-halogen bonds than the Parent do not by themselves establish improved stability or synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: Tiny fragments and enlarged repeated frameworks fail to reproduce the moderate-sized distribution of carbonyl, nitrogen and peripheral substituents found in better products. The acyclic leader prevents interpreting the observed gap as a universal need for additional rings.

The evaluated upper sample lacks chemically routine, stereochemically and geometrically defined alternatives spanning these same functional arrangements without terminal C=S, N-S or short unsaturated-ring liabilities. Their absence here does not establish absence from unscored pool support.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three Child maxima are 0.431372, 0.434190 and 0.418967. The bulky repeated dicarbonyl assembly at seed 0/evaluation 82 scores only 7.721662777993149e-34, and atomic F at seed 2/ evaluation 253 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Thus moderate size and a distributed functional-group arrangement matter within these samples; neither ring abundance nor fluorine alone is sufficient. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.431372 versus 0.651021; 0.434190 versus 0.487006; 0.418967 versus 0.720885 (rounded to six decimals).

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the current complete panel, 669 actual evaluated choices have zero marginal gain; 14 exceed their frozen accepted incumbent and 205 are later bred. Two session leaders are zero choices, including an acyclic urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl product made by appending and opening a ring. Its accepted precursor and the distinct earlier incumbent are exactly joined. This narrows the output limitation to a mismatch between some observed molecular transformations and their sampled improvement support. The historic n-9c0f6fa601f8 and n-0db88abff519 results remain conditional on their exchange-containing Parent and different allocation laws; no current-Parent unthresholded scored sibling isolates the threshold here.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically informative accepted molecules can lie outside all positive finite-panel improvement scenarios, so zero sampled value does not identify unproductive chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain chemical provenance and real feedback for novel transformations even when the finite panel assigns zero marginal value. Distinguish ring opening that retains a distributed polar framework from destructive fragmentation; neither a new chemistry ban nor a claim about unscored alternatives follows from the zero class. Any future allocation interpretation must preserve the complete-law and historical comparison limits.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry gap, reproduced by Parent n-62daf219c70a, remains with a changed balance: N-X/O-X/O-O occurrences decrease to 437/109/75, while ring carbons with at least two double bonds occur in 147 evaluated products versus Parent 42. Aryl cyanates, N-S substitution, terminal thiocarbonyl chains, short unsaturated rings and dense bridges coexist with recognizable amines, amides and ethers. Some ordinary high-value products avoid these motifs, so they are not required in every productive family. These structural counts describe selected output, not relative chemical outcomes of passive alternative batches.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably separate conventional whole-molecule alternatives from reactive substituents and difficult ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand chemically conventional alternatives preserving accepted molecules’ ring, amine and carbonyl relationships, with task-agnostic feedback assessing their value. Track explicit reactive bonds and ring geometry separately from graph validity and descriptor similarity; a lower count of one liability is not a universal feasibility gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The current evaluated stream includes 124 molecules with at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 99 and extends to 120 heavy atoms. Tiny examples often score at or near the observed floor, while a large repeated heterocyclic product scores 7.721662777993149e-34. In contrast, one ring-free 24-heavy-atom product leads its session and several compact amine or carbonyl frameworks score well. The evidence therefore concerns maintenance of a useful distributed architecture, not a universal ring-retention or size-minimization rule. This refines the existing n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a whole-molecule plausibility gap without assigning an endpoint effect to any edit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold size and functional-group relationships are not consistently preserved across fragmentation, ring edits and molecular enlargement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled changes of connectivity while retaining and contrasting complete accepted functional-group arrangements. Separate useful ring opening from collapse and avoid equating repeated motifs with useful added chemistry. Validate the actual resulting molecules through authorized feedback; unselected pool outcomes remain unknown.

transferable_gaps.evidence: As in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a, every current digest stereocentre-marker rate is zero. RDKit nevertheless finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,391 of 4,350 optimizer products, including every molecule in two highest-fifty excerpts and both saturated/cyclobutene and bridged lactam leaders. The acyclic thiocarbonyl leader also lacks specified alkene geometry. These are observations about evaluated representations, not proof that all potential configurations are stable or absent from every unscored generated structure.
transferable_gaps.gap: Evaluated stereochemical and geometric alternatives remain unspecified despite abundant saturated, bridged and heteroatom-adjacent centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve meaningful stereochemical and alkene-geometric distinctions where the actual graph supports them, then use allowed feedback to assess their value. Do not infer achirality, accessible geometry or a preferred configuration from unspecified strings and scalar scores.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
